captions.caption: Team-15 dual-robot search & rescue — a collapsed building (synthetic 48 m site). AIR-1 aerial scout + GND-1 RoverC-Pro, both running our real planners. Corridors start UNKNOWN (hatched amber).
1 · Aerial search — AIR-1 plans every move with our PR #17 Monte-Carlo tree search over a probability map. The cyan square is its real camera footprint.
2 · Survivor candidate — reported only because it fell inside the footprint. AIR-1 hovers three looks to confirm (Bayes confidence).
3 · Shared map + route check — before dispatch, the coordinator has the drone observe the rover's route. Debris it saw on M1-N1 is avoided.
4 · Handoff — GND-1 drives with our real Navigator + safety supervisor, on corridors observed CLEAR only (blue chevrons = its Dijkstra route).
5 · Dynamic event — the simulator drops debris on the planned corridor. The agents are not told (grey = ground truth, shown to the viewer only).
6 · Obstacle — the rover's ultrasonic stops it: STOP → VERIFY (3 readings) → MARK BLOCKED → SCAN. The drone is tasked to re-check the block.
7 · Cooperation — no KNOWN-clear detour (its observations are stale), so the rover holds and requests sensing. AIR-1 observes the detour.
8 · Replan — the Navigator replans with Dijkstra over corridors now observed CLEAR, then retreats along a verified path.
9 · Rescue approach — GND-1 follows the detour to the survivor's room.
10 · Safety decision — at the standoff the rover's camera (simulated) sees the survivor. The rover stops: the sighting stays UNCONFIRMED until a human reviews it.
11 · Rescue intelligence (right panel) — Qwen3.5-2B + RAG explains the mission from timestamped observation ids. Advisory only: no motor authority.
